audit_findings.title: Growth may be acquisition-funded rather than organic
audit_findings.magnitude: 2025 acquisition revenue contribution $419.9 million versus $96.0 million organic decline; base-versus-bear operating PV difference $3,699 million ($9.38/share) and bull-versus-bear difference $7,037 million ($17.84/share)
audit_findings.mechanism: Forecast growth increases owner earnings without deducting acquisition capital if acquisitions are required to produce that growth.
audit_findings.evidence: The increase in revenues was primarily due to acquisitions of $419.9 million and the favorable impact of foreign currencies of $92.0 million, partially offset by lower organic revenues of $96.0 million.
audit_findings.explanation: The acquisition-driven composition of 2025 growth is demonstrated, but it does not by itself prove that future organic growth is unavailable. The issue is material because removing assumed growth moves value from $50.14 to $40.76 per share in the base case and from $58.60 to $40.76 in the bull case.
audit_findings.action: Separate acquired and organic owner earnings for 2023-2026, identify reinvestment supporting organic growth, and rerun base and bull cases with acquisition spending deducted or growth limited to organically supportable rates.

audit_findings.title: The bridge treats all cash as excess and distributable
audit_findings.magnitude: $1,173.5 million gross cash add-back, equal to $2.97/share and 5.9% of base equity value; filed repatriation-tax liability $67.3 million, equal to $0.17/share
audit_findings.mechanism: The bridge adds gross cash to equity value without an identified deduction for operating cash, restrictions, taxes or minority ownership.
audit_findings.evidence: A substantial portion of our cash is in jurisdictions outside the United States.
audit_findings.explanation: Adding the entire balance is demonstrated, but the record does not establish how much is genuinely unavailable. The potential adjustment ranges from the identified $67.3 million tax liability to an unquantified operating, restricted and minority-owned amount, so materiality cannot be resolved from the supplied filings.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile June 30, 2026 cash by jurisdiction, legal owner and restriction; determine minimum operating cash and taxes attributable to distribution; then rerun the bridge using only common-shareholder excess cash.

audit_findings.title: Recurring restructuring costs may have been normalized away
audit_findings.magnitude: $51.4 million pre-tax in 2025, equal to 4.1% of the $1,253.1 million owner-earnings anchor; $31.2 million in 2024 and $11.9 million in the first half of 2026
audit_findings.mechanism: If recurring restructuring charges were added back, the owner-earnings anchor and historical trend omit a continuing operating cash cost.
audit_findings.evidence: We incurred restructuring charges of $51.4 million and $31.2 million in the years ended December 31, 2025 and 2024, respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: Recurring charges are demonstrated, including continued 2026 spending, but the supplied record does not show whether the owner-earnings series added them back or what normalized after-tax amount should remain. The possible valuation effect therefore remains unresolved.
audit_findings.action: Produce each annual owner-earnings reconciliation, identify restructuring amounts added back, determine a recurring after-tax normalization from filed cash charges, and rerun the anchor and scenarios if any recurring amount was excluded.

audit_findings.title: Cross-currency hedge settlements may be an omitted financing claim
audit_findings.magnitude: June 30, 2026 cross-currency-swap assets $7.8 million and liabilities $99.6 million, producing a $91.8 million net liability, equal to $0.23/share and 0.46% of base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: An unoffset derivative settlement liability would require a bridge deduction, while an economically offset net-investment hedge should not be deducted separately from the translated foreign operations.
audit_findings.evidence: These contracts expire in May 2027 and have been designated as net investment hedges of our Euro denominated subsidiaries and require an exchange of the notional amounts at maturity.
audit_findings.explanation: Whether a separate deduction is conceptually required remains unresolved, but the latest filed net liability is only $91.8 million. Even a full deduction would reduce base value by approximately $0.23 per share and would not change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile derivative assets and liabilities against the translated foreign net investments and, if the $91.8 million net liability is unoffset, rerun the bridge with that deduction.

audit_findings.title: Contingent acquisition consideration sits ahead of common equity
audit_findings.magnitude: $31.4 million at June 30, 2026, equal to $0.08/share and 0.16% of base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Contingent consideration is an acquisition-related financing claim that can avoid the operating-cash-flow owner-earnings numerator and should be deducted in the equity bridge if not otherwise charged.
audit_findings.evidence: As of December 31, 2025, the contingent consideration included in “Accrued liabilities” and “Other liabilities” on the Consolidated Balance Sheets were $ 3.5 million and $ 40.5 million, respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: The latest filing demonstrates a $31.4 million claim omitted from the stated cash-only bridge. The omission overstates value, but a full deduction changes value by only about $0.08 per share and cannot alter the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Rerun the bridge deducting the June 30, 2026 $31.4 million liability and confirm that owner earnings do not also include its fair-value remeasurement or settlement effects.

audit_findings.title: The numerator and bridge may include value owned by minority shareholders
audit_findings.magnitude: 2025 noncontrolling-interest earnings $7.4 million, equal to 0.6% of the owner-earnings anchor; June 30, 2026 carrying noncontrolling interest $65.7 million, equal to $0.17/share; minority-owned cash and economic value unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Consolidated owner earnings and cash can include 100% of controlled subsidiaries even though common shareholders own less than 100%; the minority claim must be removed from owner earnings or the bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company has a controlling interest of approximately 75 % of the common shares of Ingersoll-Rand India Limited.
audit_findings.explanation: The 75% ownership and minority claim are demonstrated, but the supplied owner-earnings reconciliation does not show whether noncontrolling earnings were removed. Carrying value is not a reliable measure of the publicly traded minority's economic claim, and subsidiary cash is undisclosed, so materiality remains unresolved.
audit_findings.action: Obtain Ingersoll-Rand India subsidiary earnings, cash, dividends and market capitalization; verify the owner-earnings adjustment for noncontrolling interests; and rerun both the numerator and cash bridge for the minority-owned portion.
